newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends up due to fall in share prices.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends up due to fall in share prices.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract rose on Friday due to a fall in share prices and a rise in Japanese government bond futures.
Traders said trade was relatively subdued ahead of Saturday's Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' meeting.
The dollar's rise to as high as 124.30 yen in Tokyo capped the December's upperside, a city bank trader said.
If the results of the G7 meeting manage to prevent a further rise in the dollar, the December will likely be stuck in a range between 99.23 and 99.33, the city bank trader said.
But if the dollar continues to rise after the G7 meeting, the December may fall as low as 99.15, the trader added.
Traders said the Economic Planning Agency's (EPA) monthly economic report for February released this morning had little effect on the market.
The EPA said in its overall assessment that while the tempo remained slow, the economy was recovering on the back of strong capital spending and housing starts.
Euroyen futures are likely to be supported by the market's view that the Bank of Japan will maintain its current low interest rate policy, a trader for a major brokerage house said.

"Judging from the current condition of the economy it will be a long time before the BOJ is able to raise short-term interest rates, and Euroyen futures will be supported by the stable and low level of interest rates," the trader said.
The BOJ injected a net 500 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining its neutral stance.
Traders said the weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.48 percent as of late afternoon on Friday, down from Thursday's 0.49 percent.
"It is a bit difficult to say at this point, but the weighted average is more likely to be 0.48 percent than 0.47 percent," a trader for another city bank said.

Certificates of deposit (CDs) were all tagged with sell quotes by late afternoon on Friday, with no new issues detected, traders said. The key three-month CDs and two-month CDs were tagged with sell quotes of 0.54 percent. One-month CDs were offered at 0.52 percent.--Tokyo Treasury Desk
